readme: Error signatures that scripts/run_stages.py recognises, and what to do about them.
Order matters: the first entry whose 'match' (a Python regex, multiline) hits the end of the stage log wins.
Fields:
id            stable name; also the argument of: run_stages.py apply-fix --fix <id>
stages        stages this applies to: check | launch | clone | deps | deb | snap | any
match         regex searched in the last 400 KB of the stage log
class         environment | wait | tooling | kernel
environment: not the workshop's fault (network, disk, memory). Stop and report; costs no repair iteration.
wait:        an operation is still running. Wait, do not relaunch.
tooling:     the workshop's own scripts, hooks or packages. May be repaired when 'ops' is present.
kernel:      the kernel source or its patches. NEVER repaired; stop and report to the user.
explain       one sentence for the repair log and the final report
ops           deterministic edits (only under .workshop/ and sdk/). Absent means: report, do not auto-fix.
restart_from  first stage to run again after the edit
ops:
delete-top-level-keys  {file: glob, keys: [..]}
restore-from-template  {files: [..]}  copy the file from assets/workshop-template/ (only files without placeholders)
fix-snapcraft          {}              build-base, architecture stanza and kernel source path from config/workshop.yaml
add-apt-packages       {packages: [..]} or, without 'packages', the names captured by the (?P<pkgs>..) group of 'match'
To add an entry: reproduce the failure, put the smallest regex that only the real cause produces, and prefer an op that restores the template over a hand-written edit.

fixes.match: No space left on device|ENOSPC|storage pool .* (is )?full
fixes.explain: The host or the workshop storage pool is out of disk space (a kernel build needs about 25 GB).
The build ran out of memory; give the workshop more RAM or lower the job count.

fixes.match: Could not resolve host|Temporary failure in name resolution|Network is unreachable|Connection timed out|503 Service Unavailable|Service Unavailable
fixes.explain: A network or archive outage. Retry later; this is not a workshop defect.
A previous launch is still running in the workshop daemon (cancelling the client does not stop it). Wait for it to finish; do not relaunch.
The installed workshop tool rejects top-level summary:/description: in a workshop definition.
snapcraft has no --project-dir option; pack.sh must cd into the project directory.
The kernel plugin is experimental in this snapcraft; pack.sh must pass --enable-experimental-plugins.

fixes.match: union_tag_not_found|'build_base' \| 'build-base'|build-on architectures .* does not match host|does not match host architecture|snapcraft-(base|build-base|architectures|platforms|build-for|source):
fixes.explain: snapcraft.yaml has the wrong shape for a kernel snap: build-base instead of base, an architecture stanza that matches the Ubuntu Core base, and source pointing at ../../../kernel-src.

fixes.match: early EOF|GnuTLS recv error|RPC failed|HTTP/2 stream .* was not closed cleanly|unexpected disconnect
fixes.explain: git.launchpad.net dropped the transfer. The template clones a tag shallowly over HTTP/1.1 with retries; restore that version of source.sh. If it is already current, the network is the cause.
Jammy 5.15 kernels need the dwarfdump package, which is separate from dwarves.

fixes.match: core standard library not found|can't find crate for .core
fixes.explain: Rust kernels need rust-src so that `make rustavailable` finds the core library.
The kernel's own Build-Depends names a toolchain package that the build host does not install.
dpkg-checkbuilddeps reports packages the build host lacks.

fixes.match: Patch failed to apply|error: patch failed|Cannot check out (tag|commit|branch)
fixes.explain: A configured patch does not apply, or the configured ref does not exist. That is the kernel or its patches, not the tooling: report it.
The kernel's config annotations disagree with the generated config. That is a kernel tree issue (see references/toolchain-notes.md); report it, do not edit the tree.
The kernel's own code failed to compile. That is the kernel source, not the tooling: report it with the log.
